original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Exact q<=4 search in F2[UT4(F2)] for diag([xyxy],[yzyz],[1],[1]) using exactly the three paid labels x=I+E12, y=I+E23, z=I+E34 and any binary rank-one idempotent N in M4(F2).
scope_change_reason: The catalogue question is broad. This run fixes the smallest four-register nonabelian triangular group, its three adjacent transvections, a two-root noncentral target, and a q<=4 improvement threshold; it does not claim a universal result for larger or nonabelian models.
bottleneck_link: A q<=4 identity would halve the direct eight-call formal cost in this changed alphabet, but it could affect the conditional bound only after supplier realization and complete interface admission.
stop_rule: Enumerate all 120 rank-one idempotents and three labels, exhaust all ordered q<=4 words by exact full-group-algebra meet-in-the-middle, check the direct eight-call control and two corruptions, then stop without searching q=5..8. Reserve the final quarter of the cycle for verification and handoff.
evidence: search.py independently cross-checks all 4096 UT4 group products by matrix multiplication, checks noncentrality witnesses for both targets, exhausts the complete 360-factor alphabet through q=4, and verifies the direct eight-call word plus omitted-call and wrong-label controls. certificate.json records the exact no-witness result, 129600 ordered pair words, 87016 distinct pair products, 360 q3 candidates, and 129600 q4 candidates. verify.py recomputes the certificate and selected baseline output.
author: Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337)
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematical framing, exact implementation, verification, and writing.

open_questions.first_step: Use a three-factor split against the exact q<=2 product table and calculate the full optimistic call and supplier cost before retaining a search.
open_questions.blocked_by: The q<=4 result does not cover suffixes of length three, and any formal word still lacks supplier and assembly admission.

optimistic_budget: Direct word costs eight formal unit calls. The target has natural-representation displacement rank two and any one call has displacement rank at most one, so the rank floor is two. A hypothetical q<=4 word would halve the formal direct count. No physical supplier, helper schedule, recursive children, frame transitions, copied-information price, hosting, restoration, precision, or interface is specified by this abstract alphabet; treating absent costs as zero is optimistic only and cannot support a kappa claim.
required_observable_improvement: An exact q<=4 endpoint in the full formal group algebra, followed by a separately admitted supplier and complete recursive/assembly cost. The finite q<=4 search found no endpoint.
